reproduction_manifest.notes: Reproduced the random baseline compatibility score on gapminder data. The random baseline (0.142 +/- 0.727, n=15) matches the paper's reported random baseline (0.155 +/- 0.678) and falls within the rubric CI [-0.151, 0.413]. The compatibility score computation pipeline is fully functional and validated against synthetic experiments. The exact Gemma 3 4B IT result (0.131) cannot be reproduced without AWS Bedrock access to generate LLM causal coefficient matrices.
reproduction_manifest.eval_output_format: JSON block at end of stdout with keys: compatibility_score_random_baseline_mean, compatibility_score_random_baseline_std
reproduction_manifest.known_levers: The random baseline std (sigma parameter) controls score variance; increasing n_runs improves estimate stability; using actual LLM-generated coefficients (via Bedrock API) would produce paper-comparable results; the correlation matrix can be replaced with real gapminder data for exact paper match
reproduction_manifest.setup_notes: Dependencies: numpy, pandas, matplotlib, networkx, tqdm, boto3 installed via pip. Gapminder data generated synthetically from paper's Table 1 correlation matrix (PSD-corrected, max diff 0.018 from paper). Data stored in /repo/data/ as per-panel CSV files. No AWS Bedrock credentials configured. Hugging Face models inaccessible due to network restrictions in container.

optimization_objective.summary: Maximize the compatibility score for bivariate causal statements on gapminder data. Higher scores indicate more internally consistent causal claims. The score is computed from the gapminder correlation matrix and a matrix A of bivariate causal coefficients. Optimization levers include: using better LLMs to generate coefficient matrices, tuning LLM temperature/top_p parameters, or directly optimizing coefficient values.

metrics.name: compatibility_score_random_baseline
metrics.rationale: Compatibility score quantifies how well a set of bivariate causal statements cohere into a plausible multivariate model. Paper demonstrates that better LLMs produce higher scores. Random baseline is the fallback metric when LLM access is unavailable.

optimization_objective.success_policy: Improve the compatibility score above the random baseline. For SOTA optimization, the most impactful approach is to obtain actual LLM-generated causal coefficient matrices (via Bedrock or local model) and compute compatibility scores from those. Direct numerical optimization of coefficient matrices is also possible but must respect the paper's evaluation protocol.
